signals.title: Quiles crowned Moto3 World Champion with Mandalika victory
signals.summary: The sensational 18-year-old is the latest young talent to life the World Championship with a stunning five rounds to spare The Championship race is over as victory for Maximo Quiles (CFMOTO Gaviota Aspar Team) secured the Moto3 World Championship for the Spaniard. A glittering campaign of ten wins so far, he led from Lap 2 onwards, pulled out an advantage and never looked back for one of his most dominant wins of the season ahead of nearest challenger David Almansa (Liqui Moly Dynavolt Intact GP) and Brian Uriarte (Red Bull KTM Ajo). From P2 on the grid it was a perfect launch to grab the holeshot for Almansa whilst Quiles was already into P2 on Lap 1. However, it was a barnstorming second lap that saw the gloves really come off, with Quiles in the lead as Adrian Fernandez (Leopard Racing) battled his way into the podium places. The rough and tumble was starting to fragment the group and Almansa was the rider who was paying the price; with title rival Quiles leading, Almansa was down to P8. On Lap 3, it was Grand Prix done for Casey O’Gorman (SIC58 Squadra Corse) who crashed at Turn 5, whilst teammate Leo Rammerstorfer joined him in a separate incident. Further round the lap, Ryota Ogiwara (CODE Motorsports) came to grief whilst back in the lead pack, Almansa was back into P2 by Lap 5. A mistake by Quiles at Turn 16 gave the chasing pack hope, the gap to chief title rival Almansa down to 1.6s. Half GP distance complete and things had started to spread out with Quiles 1.5s clear of Almansa, Fernandez and Alvaro Carpe (Red Bull KTM Ajo) who in-turn were 1.6s clear of Rico Salmela (Red Bull KTM Tech3). On Lap 11, disaster for Carpe who tagged the back of Fernandez and crashed at Turn 10 and although the #31 could continue, he was back in the group behind and then made a mistake at Turn 2 a lap later. More drama at the end of the lap, this time for Adrian Cruces (CIP GreenPower) who crashed at Turn 16 but was able to rejoin. Lap 14 and two seconds out front, Champion-designate Quiles picked up a track limits warning, the #28 had no room for error. With a 2.8s advantage with two laps to go though, he had the margin to relax and keep it wheels in line, despite Almansa’s efforts. Across the line and doing it in the most Quiles style possible, the Championship leader became the World Champion with a tenth victory of the season and with five rounds remaining. A magnificent campaign going to a deserving World Champion whilst Almansa was a solid second and strengthens his grasp on P2 overall. Third went the way of Brian Uriarte (Red Bull KTM Ajo) after the Spaniard pounced to pass Matteo Bertelle (LEVELUP-MTA) on the final lap. The Spanish rider lifts the title trophy in Indonesia with five rounds to spare after a dominant second season in the World Championship Salmela matched his career-best result in fifth ahead of home-hero Veda Pratama (Honda Team Asia), whereas Guido Pini (Leopard Racing) resisted teammate Fernandez for P7 at the line but due to a shortcut at Turn 9, was given a Long Lap Penalty equivalent so was P8 in the end. Joel Esteban (LEVELUP-MTA) was ninth whilst Scott Ogden (CIP GreenPower) completed the top ten. Quiles taking the title with five rounds remaining puts him in an exclusive club of riders who have done that across all classes. Mike Hailwood, Giacomo Agostini and Marc Marquez were the only three that had managed it but now, Maximo Quiles’ name is part of a unique club of riders. The title race is done but with five rounds still to go, plenty of battles remain in 2026! signals.title: Maximo Quiles: meet the 2026 Moto3 World Champion!
signals.summary: The #28 seals the deal with a win – get to know the newest Moto3 World Champion and future Moto2 star after a landmark season Maximo Quiles (CFMOTO Gaviota Aspar Team) is the 2026 Moto3 World Champion! The #28 has shown incredible pace and expert racecraft all season to secure the crown, sealing the deal with a stylish win at the Pertamina Grand Prix of Indonesia. He’s only the fourth rider in history to ever win a Championship – in any class – with five races remaining, alongside Marc Marquez, Giacomo Agostini and Mike Hailwood. The Spanish rider lifts the title trophy in Indonesia with five rounds to spare after a dominant second season in the World Championship Quiles, born in 2008, began his racing career at a young age, making headlines on minibikes before climbing through the Spanish ranks. The #28’s talent was clear, as he found himself in the MotoJunior paddock, making his European Cup debut in 2021. Incredible. The only word that comes close to describing his rookie season. Three victories, five podiums and plenty of encouraging signs. Backing that pace up the following two seasons, Quiles returned to the top step in 2022 before setting up a title attack in 2023. The Spanish star joined Aspar, winning five times and proving he was the real deal; the #28 took the 2023 European Cup crown. There was a change of scenery in 2024 as he made the step up to the Moto3 Junior World Championship. Quiles impressed instantly, winning at the season finale and clinching third in the standings. Alongside his efforts in the MotoJunior paddock, he raced in the Red Bull MotoGP Rookies Cup for three seasons. Finishing third in the Championship on two occasions and picking up seven wins from his time in the class, Quiles’ name wasn’t far from the headlines. Aspar had seen enough, signing the #28 for the 2025 season – Quiles was Moto3 World Championship bound. His rookie campaign was nothing short of incredible. His season didn’t get underway until COTA, with Quiles initially being too young to race in the opening two rounds. P5 on debut before a training crash forced the rookie to miss two rounds, returning in France. It didn’t take long for the ball to get rolling either, with Quiles earning podiums at Silverstone and Aragon before a maiden win at Mugello. Ending 2025 with three wins, nine podiums and two pole positions was an impressive addition to his CV, and set up a title attack… 2026 couldn’t have started much better for Quiles, winning four of the opening six races and standing on the podium a further two times. Further wins in Hungary and Assen only upped his Championship momentum – bringing his lead to 104 points – as we reached the summer break in Germany. However, it wasn’t all smooth sailing for the title leader, crashing in Q2 at Silverstone and sitting out the remainder of the weekend after a collarbone break. His comeback and response? Winning the next round at MotorLand Aragon to make his intentions clear – the title attack wasn’t over. Quiles carried his incredible form to Misano and Austria, making it three consecutive race wins, extending his lead to 131 points and setting up his first match point in Japan. His future might already be decided, with the Spanish sensation confirming the move to Moto2 next season, but his mission in Moto3 wasn’t over yet. The deal wasn’t sealed just yet though. A second place in Motegi, under the pressure of his first match point, was impressive – but closest title rival David Almansa (Liqui Moly Dynavolt Intact GP) made a stunning last stand to make Quiles wait for it. The #28’s moment in the spotlight then finally arrived at the Indonesian GP. Quiles was right at the front from the off, escaped a huge group scuffle for the podium and kept it calm to the line for his 10 th win of the season, crowning himself 2026 Moto3 World Champion. signals.title: Hat-trick hero: Guevara wins dramatic Mandalika battle as gap tightens to Gonzalez
signals.summary: The #28 capitalises on late heartbreak for race leader Escrig to make it three victories on the spin, but the #18 produces a fine comeback to lose just five points in Indonesia How about that for a drama-drenched Moto2 race at the Pertamina Grand Prix of Indonesia? Coming out on top, for the third time in a row, was red-hot Izan Guevara (BLU CRU Pramac Yamaha Moto2) as the title race gap between the Spaniard and Manuel Gonzalez (Liqui Moly Dynavolt Intact GP) reduces further – but not by much. Gonzalez limited the damage done with a fine ride to P2, while after late heartbreak arrives for race leader Alex Escrig (KLINT Racing Team) on the penultimate lap, Daniel Holgado (CFMOTO Power Electronics Aspar Team) – who was involved in a four-rider, red-flagged Turn 1 crash – ends his weekend with a return to podium ways. As we went racing in Moto2, there was immediate drama at Turn 1. Four riders were down, including both CFMOTO Power Electronics Aspar Team riders in David Alonso and Holgado, with the latter tagging the back of his teammate into the opening corner to send the duo down. Alonso was brutally launched into the air, while Joe Roberts (OnlyFans American Racing Team) had nowhere to go on the outside line and collected the stricken bike of Holgado’s, sending the American sliding down the road too. Collin Veijer (Red Bull KTM Ajo) was then left with no option but to run into the barrel-rolling, out-of-control Kalex-Triumph of Alonso, which caused Veijer to crash at Turn 1 too. Here's what happened in Turn 1 🔎 Thankfully all riders are on their feet 👏 #IndonesianGP 🇮🇩 https://t.co/XLaars53Bx Thankfully, all four riders were able to return to the pit lane and were relatively unscathed after the red flags were shown. Unfortunately for Alonso, with the fuel tank being ripped out in the crash, amongst other significant bike damage, his Sunday in Indonesia wouldn’t be restarted. Rotten luck for the Colombian. There were better fortunes for Holgado, Roberts, and Veijer though – all three left pit lane in time to take up their spots on the restart grid, but Roberts then peeled back into the box before lights out. Clearly something wasn’t quite right on the American’s machine, and we subsequently learned it was a rear brake problem. Just like Alonso, a slice of terrible luck for Roberts. There were no such issues for Escrig, though. The Spaniard grabbed the holeshot to dip his wheels ahead of Guevara at the start, with Holgado third before Ivan Ortola (QJMOTOR – JP Financial – MSI) battled past the #96. That changed hands again on Lap 2 with Gonzalez pouncing up to P6, then P5, as we clicked onto Lap 3. By Lap 6, a clear top five had formed. Escrig led Guevara by 0.8s, Holgado held P3 and sat 0.8s behind Guevara’s rear tyre, with fourth place Ortola being caught by Gonzalez. And soon enough, P4 was now in the hands of the championship leader on Lap 7. P4 became P3 for Gonzalez not too long after. Holgado didn’t have the pace to remain in the podium-paying positions, and with five laps to go, the title race frontrunner sat in the bronze medal position. Three seconds up the road, Guevara was making moves too. No passes yet, but the #28 was beginning to reel in race leader Escrig. But Escrig did then pick up the pace on Lap 12 of 14. We were about to strap in for a proper fight for the win in Indonesia between Escrig and Guevara for the win, before a technical issue halted Escrig’s Lombok stormer. Cruel in the extreme. Escrig’s wonderful weekend ended with a woeful bit of luck, and that allowed Guevara to take over the P1 baton. And he didn’t flinch. A hat-trick of wins for Guevara, as the gap to Gonzalez comes down again – but only by five points as the #18 bounces back from a disappointing Saturday to earn 20 crucial points in this compelling title chase. 6.5 points now the margin. Third went to Holgado after Escrig’s technical problem, and after his Turn 1 crash, his rollercoaster Sunday ends on a high. Senna Agius (Liqui Moly Dynavolt Intact GP) was another rider, like his teammate, who delivered a classy comeback ride on Sunday. The Australian clinched P4 from P13 on the grid, with Daniel Muñoz (Italtrans Racing Team) closing out the top five ahead of Ortola. Filip Salač (OnlyFans American Racing Team) crossed the line in P7, 1.6s clear of Alonso Lopez (ITALJET Gresini Moto2), Tony Arbolino (REDS Fantic Racing), and Jose Antonio Rueda (Red Bull KTM Tech3) – those were the riders closing out the top 10 in Indonesia. signals.title: Bezzecchi beats Fernandez in Mandalika as Martin returns to championship summit
signals.summary: The Italian keeps his title hopes alive with a first victory since Mugello, with Aprilia making history in Indonesia to see Marc Marquez finish outside of the top five 300 MotoGP wins for Italy. A history-making Aprilia top-four lockout. And a first victory since the Italian Grand Prix for Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia Racing). That result, after the drama bubbled over in the Mandalika cauldron on Saturday, was desperately needed as Bezzecchi claws back crucial ground in the championship chase. Second place went to the heroic Raul Fernandez (SuperFile Trackhouse MotoGP Team), who, despite two broken fingers, climbed onto the podium, while Jorge Martin (Aprilia Racing) pocketed P3 to retake the World Championship lead after Marc Marquez (Ducati Lenovo Team) came home in P6. Unlike in the Tissot Sprint, Turn 1 in the Grand Prix was attacked and negotiated without incident. Bezzecchi lunged up the inside of Fernandez to try and gobble up the holeshot and take the lead, but the Italian was slightly wide on the exit to allow the polesitter back through. Marc Marquez got away well, the Sprint winner was an early P3, with 2025 Indonesia winner Fermin Aldeguer (BK8 Gresini Racing MotoGP) getting the better of Martin to grab P5, and then P4 from Fabio Di Giannantonio (Pertamina Enduro VR46 Racing Team). Martin then picked his way past Di Giannantonio to move up to P5, before the fast-starting Aldeguer slipped out of contention at the tricky Turn 16 on Lap 2. That gave Martin a free pass to move into P4, but what wasn’t a free pass was what came half a lap later. Martin, on the inside of Marc Marquez at Turn 10, fired his Aprilia through to climb ahead of his title rival. It was P3 for Martin now, P4 for Marquez, with Pedro Acosta (Red Bull KTM Factory Racing) now hunting the pre-race World Championship leader. And on Lap 4, Acosta set the fastest lap of the Grand Prix. It felt like it had been coming for a couple of laps, and sure enough, Acosta pounced on the championship leader. Teammates next year. No teamwork this year, though. Acosta lunged at Turn 10, super late on the anchors, but boy did he nail the pass. A moment on the front-end came through Turn 11 for Acosta, but the #37 held onto P4 to shuffle Marc Marquez back to P5, and in the clutches of Di Giannantonio. At the front, Fernandez held Bezzecchi at bay by 0.5s, with Martin lapping 1.9s away from his teammate’s rear Michelin tyre. It was as you were for a few laps before Bezzecchi netted the fastest lap of the Grand Prix, a 1:29.991, to begin adding some pressure to Fernandez. 0.4s was the slender gap, with Martin now 2.5s back. On Lap 13, Marc Marquez was back ahead of Acosta. From the TV pictures, it looked like Acosta was forced to allow his 2027 teammate through, which seemingly meant tyre pressure problems were arising for the KTM star. Then, two laps later, the switch came at Turn 10. Was Marc Marquez now suffering from tyre pressure problems? Incredible. Back at the front. Lap 19 of 27, the lead changed for the first time since Turn 1, Lap 1. Bezzecchi carved his way past Fernandez to snatch the lead from the Trackhouse star, and on that very same lap, the Italian hammered home another fastest lap of the Grand Prix. With Fernandez running a little wide at Turn 1 after the move, Bezzecchi’s lead grew to an immediate 1.4s, with Martin riding in a lonely P3 – 2.4s behind Fernandez, 5.7s clear of the popcorn-consuming fight between Acosta, Marc Marquez, and now Ai Ogura (SuperFile Trackhouse MotoGP Team). Sure enough, the Japanese star pounced. Marc Marquez was shoved back to P6 on Lap 21 at Turn 16, as Ogura then set his sights on trying to make a move on Acosta. His teammate wasn’t giving Martin a sniff at P2 a little further up the road; Fernandez was digging in deep to maintain the gap to Martin, as Ogura then clawed his way past Acosta. Not without a fightback from Acosta though. The KTM star returned the favour into Turn 13, but Ogura got the job done into Turn 16. Both needed to be careful not to beat each other up too much though, because the #93 was lurking. Last lap time then in Indonesia. Bezzecchi’s 3.3s lead meant the Italian could cruise to the flag to earn a much-needed victory, his first since Mugello, to keep his slim title hopes well and truly alive. Chapeau to Fernandez. With not one, but two broken fingers sustained in the Sprint crash yesterday, Fernandez went above and beyond the call of duty to pocket P2 in Indonesia and also extracting the maximum from Sunday was Martin. The championship leader again. Two points the gap. As you were coming into the weekend. Martin’s 16 points were critical in Mandalika. And handing Aprilia their very first MotoGP 1-2-3-4 finish was Ogura, who did manage to fend off Acosta at the end of the Grand Prix. What a day for the Noale factory. Acosta finished just a tenth away from Ogura to bag a hard-fought P5 in Mandalika, and just over a second behind the battle was Marc Marquez. P6 at the flag means the #93 slides back into P2 in the title chase, but the seven-time MotoGP World Champion would have taken a two-point deficit at the beginning of the weekend. Why? Because he’d never even finished a Grand Prix in Indonesia. And such was Aprilia’s superiority here; not losing any ground to Martin signals a job well done ahead of a trip to Phillip Island. Alex Marquez (BK8 Gresini Racing MotoGP) and Di Giannantonio crossed the line in P7 and P8, with the Italian only just holding off ninth-place Fabio Quartararo (Monster Energy Yamaha MotoGP). P10 went to Enea Bastianini (Red Bull KTM Tech3), with the other points going to Brad Binder (Red Bull KTM Factory Racing) in P12, Johann Zarco (Castrol Honda LCR) in P13, Franco Morbidelli (Pertamina Enduro VR46 Racing Team) in P14, and Alex Rins (Monster Energy Yamaha MotoGP) in P15. Indonesia hosted its fair share of drama. And as we look ahead to our final date with the beautiful Phillip Island, the title race remains finely poised. Two points sepa

signals.title: Uriarte turns up the magic in Mandalika as title rivals lock out the front row
signals.summary: The Red Bull KTM Ajo rookie claims a season third pole ahead of Almansa and Carpe, leaving match-point man Quiles sixth Brian Uriarte (Red Bull KTM Ajo) lit up Mandalika with a sensational Saturday charge, grabbing his third pole position of the year and planting himself right at the heart of the title fight. Alongside him, fellow contenders David Almansa (Liqui Moly Dynavolt Intact GP) and Alvaro Carpe (Red Bull KTM Ajo) completed a blockbuster front row. A trio of challengers perfectly placed to spoil Maximo Quiles’ match point party in Lombok. With track temperatures at a steamy 65ºC, Uriarte wasted little time laying down the benchmark. The rookie fired in a 1:36.861 on his third lap to go 0.355s clear of Championship leader Maximo Quiles (CFMOTO Gaviota Aspar Team), and even a breathless final-lap shootout couldn’t prise pole away from the #51. Quiles’ session hit a snag at the halfway mark. The Spaniard suffered a slow crash at Turn 16, but with his KTM still running, he quickly picked it up and headed straight back to the pits. With 7 minutes remaining, the entire field was back in pit lane, the provisional front row featured Uriarte, Quiles and Matteo Bertelle (LEVEL UP – MTA), while Almansa languished down in P10. With just three minutes to go, it was the Liqui Moly Dynavolt Intact rider who led the field back out for one final attack, triggering a train of riders desperate to claim their spot on the front row. David Muñoz (Liqui Moly Dynavolt Intact GP) was still without a valid lap at that stage, while Rico Salmela (Red Bull KTM Tech3), who had suffered a Turn 10 crash at the 10 minute mark, was unable to rejoin the fight and had to settle for 16th. Then came the final-lap fireworks. Casey O’Gorman (SIC58 Squadra Corse) went down at the first turn, while Bertelle lit up Sector 1 and Adrian Fernandez (Leopard Racing) set the session’s best second sector. Almansa delivered when it mattered most, jumping to second with a 1:36.948, only 0.087s slower than Uriarte. Fernandez briefly put himself onto the front row before Carpe struck back. The Red Bull KTM Ajo rider produced a 1:37.104 on his final lap to snatch third, just 0.243s from his teammate, pushing Fernandez to fourth and Quiles all the way down to sixth. Fernandez will head row two from teammate and Guido Pini (Leopard Racing) and Quiles, whose 1:37.216 left him 0.355s from pole. Home favourite Veda Pratama (Honda Team Asia) claimed seventh ahead of Bertelle and Adrian Cruces (CIP Green Power), with O’Gorman completing the top ten. Earlier, Scott Ogden (CIP Green Power) eventually topped Q1 with a 1:37.736, ahead of Hakim Danish (AEON Credit – MT Helmets – MSI), Muñoz and Leo Rammerstorfer (SIC58 Squadra Corse), who edged Valentin Perrone (Red Bull KTM Tech3) out of the final Q2 spot by just 0.003s. For Quiles, Sunday is match point once again, but he'll have to work hard to recover various positions on the grid. Victory guarantees him the lightweight crown, while second will also be enough providing he finishes ahead of Almansa. But with all three of his title rivals locking out the front row and Quiles starting from sixth, nothing about this one looks straightforward. One clean getaway could seal the Championship, one twist at Mandalika could send the fight roaring on to Australia. Everything is set for a huge Moto3 Sunday. signals.title: Marc Marquez wins dramatic Mandalika Sprint, Martin loses the lead after rollercoaster ride to fourth
signals.summary: The #93 emerges victorious in Indonesia, with Turn 1 drama for Bezzecchi and a dramatic Saturday afternoon for Martin seeing a new championship leader take over on top Marc Marquez (Ducati Lenovo Team) takes home gold on Saturday at the Pertamina Grand Prix of Indonesia, taking the lead in the Championship after a dramatic Tissot Sprint saw early leader Jorge Martin (Aprilia Racing) drop back, run off and then come home fourth. That was after Turn 1 drama off the start that sidelined Marco Bezzechi (Aprilia Racing) and polesitter Raul Fernandez (SuperFile Trackhouse MotoGP Team), changing the game early on after lights out. Ai Ogura (SuperFile Trackhouse MotoGP Team) took second on the Sprint podium after escaping the drama early on, with Fabio Di Giannantonio (Pertamina Enduro VR46 Racing Team) taking third. LIGHTS OUT, DRAMA ON There was immediate drama at Turn 1 as Fernandez vs Bezzecchi started as a drag race and then became a crunch, with Marc Marquez and Di Giannantonio both heading up the inside too. The top four all headed slightly wide and then the knock on effect saw Diggia sitting up make Marc Marquez sit up and then Bezzecchi left with nowhere to go, crashing out alongside polesitter Fernandez. Riders ok. As all that was happening, Martin carved around the apex and took the lead, in position to stake a strong claim on the 12 points for the win. Behind him, Marc Marquez was holding second, with emerging in third ahead of Diggia after the #49 had slotted back in in fourth, defending it from Alex Marquez (BK8 Gresini Racing MotoGP). DUEL AT THE FRONT? As the laps ticked down, it seemed a duel at the front as the #93 loomed large behind race leader Martin, but the Aprilia got the hammer down and started to build a gap, well over a second clear. But then drama suddenly as the #89 sat up with 4 laps to go, losing more than two seconds in the lap and watching Marquez take over in the lead. Meanwhile, Pedro Acosta (Red Bull KTM Factory Racing) was given a long lap for track limits, dropping him off the back of Diggia, Ogura and the podium fight. Martin slotted back in just ahead of the Japanese rider in that battle, but then the #89 started to reel in Sprint leader Marc Marquez once more. With three to go, the Aprilia was homing in and target locked on the leading Ducati – but he was bringing company. Suddenly, the pendulum then swung back. As the title gap hovered at a single point, Martin was wide and off the circuit as he was forced into a save at Turn 15 – dropping out of the podium fight and leaving Ogura and Di Giannantonio to chase down the #93. The #89 was back in fourth. THE LAST PUSH TO THE LINE The metres were ticking down at the front but Ogura gave it a good run. The #79 halved the gap on the final lap then couldn’t quite make it to striking distance, leaving Marc Marquez to cross the line for his first Sprint win at Mandalika. Ogura’s P2 moves him to within a point of Acosta in fourth in the title fight, with Di Giannantonio completing the Saturday podium. Then comes Martin. After leading the way and convincingly pulling away, dropping back and then ultimately losing out on the rostrum late on, the gap is now four points – and it’s now in favour of Marc Marquez at the top. Alex Marquez takes P5 in some fresh air, with Acosta completing the top six after that Long Lap penalty for track limits. Fermin Aldeguer (BK8 Gresini Racing MotoGP), the 2025 GP winner here, slots into P7 ahead of Francesco Bagnaia (Ducati Lenovo Team) and the scorer of the final point: Fabio Quartararo (Monster Energy Yamaha MotoGP). That’s it from Sprint Saturday, but there’s plenty more to come on Sunday. Marc Marquez now leads the Championship by four points ahead of Martin – and a win takes 25 the 20 for second place. It can all change again tomorrow, with more laps, Bezzechi and Fernandez back in business, and another rollercoaster ready to race. signals.title: Guevara soars to incredible Indonesia pole, title rival Gonzalez P10
signals.summary: The first-ever 1:31 Moto2 lap time was slammed home in a Mandalika qualifying stunner that has big championship implications What a lap. What a session. For the fifth time in 2026, title-hunting Izan Guevara (BLU CRU Pramac Yamaha Moto2) will launch from pole position for the Moto2 Grand Prix thanks to a stunning 1:31.963 – the very first Moto2 lap in the 1:31 bracket. It was a rollercoaster Q2 that saw Alex Escrig (KLINT Racing Team) clinch P2, the Spaniard only 0.098s away from pole, with Colombia’s David Alonso (CFMOTO Power Electronics Aspar Team) leaving it late to jump up to the front row. The other headline grabber? Manuel Gonzalez (Liqui Moly Dynavolt Intact GP). The World Championship leader will be starting from P10 on Lombok, having lapped 0.413s slower than his chief title rival in a blockbuster 15-minute Qualifying 2 session. Escrig occupied provisional pole for much of the session, but Guevara rolled out that stunner to steal the Saturday honours – and a Tissot watch! – away from the KLINT star. Alonso shoved teammate Daniel Holgado off the front row in the latter stages; it’s P4 for the #96, while Daniel Muñoz (Italtrans Racing Team) and the rider third in the championship, Ivan Ortola (QJMOTOR – JP Financial – MSI), line up in P5 and P6 respectively. Having come through Q1, both Joe Roberts (OnlyFans American Racing Team) and recently injured Collin Veijer (Red Bull KTM Ajo) should be satisfied with P7 and P8 in Q2, with Japanese GP podium finisher Tony Arbolino (REDS Fantic Racing) joining the American and Dutchman on Row 3. Then comes Gonzalez. It’s a disappointing day for the title race leader, who now has plenty of pressure on to try and keep his 10.5-point lead afloat on Sunday. signals.title: Fernandez clinches maiden MotoGP pole, Marc Marquez and Martin off front row
signals.summary: A fascinating qualifying unfolds in Indonesia as Bezzecchi and Di Giannantonio join the SuperFile Trackhouse star on the front row For the first time in MotoGP, Raul Fernandez (SuperFile Trackhouse MotoGP Team) will launch from pole position as a tantalising qualifying scrap unfolds at the Pertamina Grand Prix of Indonesia. It’s an Aprilia 1-2 at the spearhead of the grid thanks to Marco Bezzecchi’s (Aprilia Racing) efforts, the Italian 0.109s adrift of Fernandez’s 1:28.852, and denying Jorge Martin (Aprilia Racing) and Marc Marquez (Ducati Lenovo Team) a front row start on Lombok was a rather rapid birthday boy on Saturday morning – Fabio Di Giannantonio (Pertamina Enduro VR46 Racing Team) the rider to join Fernandez and Bezzecchi on the front row. Straight out of the qualifying crate, 2025 Indonesian GP winner Fermin Aldeguer (BK8 Gresini Racing MotoGP) set his best lap of the weekend to top the early running in the opening 15-minute time attack stint, before his time was beaten by Ai Ogura (SuperFile Trackhouse MotoGP Team). A 1:29.729 saw the Japanese rider rise above Aldeguer by 0.016s before Aldeguer returned to P1 by 0.090s, as Ogura then crashed in the closing stages at Turn 12 to see his session end prematurely. And sitting in P2, would Ogura keep his Q2 promotion place? It was a session of attrition in Q1. Johann Zarco (Castrol Honda LCR), who crashed on his first flying lap at Turn 1, and Jack Miller (Prima Pramac Yamaha MotoGP) crashed at Turn 2 within a second of each other. Elsewhere, Enea Bastianini (Red Bull KTM Tech3) hit the deck at Turn 1, and Diogo Moreira (Pro Honda LCR) was also a crasher at the opening corner too. All of this did mean Ogura kept his top two place, with Aldeguer sailing through too. A quick shoutout too for Toprak Razgatlioglu (Prima Pramac Yamaha MotoGP). Less than an hour after dislocating his right shoulder in FP2, the Turk qualified less than a second off Aldeguer’s top time in Q1. Chapeau. At the end of the first flyers in the battle for pole, Marc Marquez led Bezzecchi by 0.025s as the title chasers set 1:29.2s, but the pace was about to turn up a notch or two. Di Giannantonio briefly climbed to P2 before Bezzecchi fired home a 1:28.961 to sail to provisional pole, with Fernandez slotting into second place – 0.211s away from the Italian. The first two time attack efforts from Martin didn’t go as planned. The title race leader sat P7, 0.814s adrift of his teammate. And heading out for the final six minutes of qualifying in Indonesia, Martin was shadowed by Marc Marquez. In other words, the top two in 2026’s title race thriller were together, and having been given the message that he was being followed by the #93, Martin couldn’t shake off the seven-time MotoGP World Champion from his tailpipes. Just ahead of duo on track was Fernandez, and it was the Practice pacesetter who set a 1:28.852 to go P1. Martin and Marc Marquez both improved, the Ducati star slightly quicker, with the championship top two sat P4 and P5 in the session with three minutes to go as Di Giannantonio leapt back onto the front row. Bezzecchi was then setting the timing screens alight, but his lap was halted after Aldeguer crashed at Turn 16. That brought out the yellow flags, but there was enough time left on the clock for Bez to have another bite at the cherry. An improvement didn’t come on his latest attempt, though. Had the life from that soft rear Michelin disappeared? What had gone was Marc Marquez’s pole and front row chances. Despite a session-best first split, the time went away in the second split, and with that, Q2 drew to a close. Fernandez will launch from his first MotoGP pole position in the Tissot Sprint and Grand Prix in Indonesia, with Bezzecchi and Di Giannantonio joining the Trackhouse star on the front row. A blockbuster Row 2 sees Marc Marquez launch from P4, Martin fires away from P5, and 2025 winner Aldeguer go from P6. Ogura recovered from his Q1 crash to qualify in P7 to sit ahead of Alex Marquez (BK8 Gresini Racing MotoGP) and Pedro Acosta (Red Bull KTM Factory Racing) on the grid, the top nine split by half a second, while Francesco Bagnaia (Ducati Lenovo Team), Franco Morbidelli (Pertamina Enduro VR46 Racing Team), and Fabio Quartararo (Monster Energy Yamaha MotoGP) make up P10, P11, and P12 on the grid. That’s an intriguing grid, isn’t it? The top two in the title race off the front row, with the stakes incredibly high going into this afternoon. Don't miss it. 15:00 local time. signals.title: On song Guevara soars to lap record Friday top spot in Indonesia
signals.summary: The recent back-to-back winner turns up the wick again to lay down the gauntlet to title rival Gonzalez heading into the weekend Winner in Austria. Winner in Japan. And now the all-time lap record holder in Moto2 after the opening day of action at the Pertamina Grand Prix of Indonesia. Those accolades go to Izan Guevara (BLU CRU Pramac Yamaha Moto2) as the rider second in the title chase lays down the gauntlet in Practice with a 1:32.337, 0.231s quicker than second-fastest Alex Escrig (KLINT Racing Team). Third place in a red-flagged Practice session went to Daniel Holgado (CFMOTO Power Electronics Aspar Team), despite the #96 encountering a technical issue in the closing stages of Friday’s running. It was Gonzalez, the World Championship leader, who finished the session in P4, 0.259s adrift of his title rival. signals.title: Fernandez flies to P1 to beat Bezzecchi and Martin on Friday
signals.summary: Aprilia rule the Mandalika roost on Friday but it’s not the two title contenders with the upper hand Raul Fernandez (SuperFile Trackhouse MotoGP Team) was the fastest on Friday at Mandalika with the Spaniard setting a new all-time lap record to lead the charge into the rest of the weekend. A 1’28.725 perches the British GP winner on top in what was a crash-strewn session, leading Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia Racing) and his Championship-leading teammate Jorge Martin with the Aprilias in mighty form, locking out the top three for the first time in Practice history. FIRST HALF: Aldeguer and Quartararo crash The first half of the session saw a couple of sizeable spills with 2025 Indonesian GP winner Fermin Aldeguer (BK8 Gresini Racing MotoGP) falling at the last corner before a fast one for Fabio Quartararo (Monster Energy Yamaha MotoGP Team) at Turn 9. Both were OK and soon back out in the second half of the session, with ‘El Diablo’ consolidating a provisional Q2 spot. Into the second half of the session and it was Fernandez who took over at the top ahead of Di Giannantonio. Bezzecchi was sitting in third whilst Marc Marquez and Franco Morbidelli (Pertamina Enduro VR46 Racing Team) rounded out the top five. Fast laps were needed by Alex Marquez (BK8 Gresini Racing MotoGP), Diogo Moreira (Pro Honda LCR) and Francesco Bagnaia (Ducati Lenovo Team), all outside the top ten with 15 minutes on the clock. MORE FALLERS: Bastianini, Moreira, Alex Marquez and Rins Going into the business end of the session, Enea Bastianini (Red Bull KTM Tech3) suffered a fast fall at Turn 9, almost identical to Quartararo’s earlier in the session. The Beast was back up on his feet and rushing back to the pits, needing to get back to the track ASAP as he was stuck in P17. Fernandez lowered the benchmark again with a 1’29.252 before repeating it a lap later with a 1’28.725, a new all-time lap record. Marc Marquez moved into P2 before a big moment into Turn 1 whereas elsewhere, Aldeguer’s Ducati ground to a halt in the gravel. Also in the gravel after a fast Turn 11 crash, Moreira’s session was over, leaving the Brazilian in Q1. More improvements came with a flurry in the final moments, with both Jorge Martin (Aprilia Racing) and Jack Miller (Prima Pramac Yamaha MotoGP) moving into P3 and P10 respectively. Alex Marquez was the latest crasher at Turn 16, leaving him in P7 and vulnerable whereas just moments later, Alex Rins (Monster Energy Yamaha MotoGP Team) was down at the final corner, likewise vulnerable with him P99. Then, Bastianini went down for a second time in what was a Friday afternoon to forget. With the chequered flag out, nobody could get near Fernandez’s new lap record, the Spaniard with a 0.219s advantage over Bezzecchi. They were the only two riders able to get into the 1’28s, with Martin more than a quarter of a second back of his teammate in third. Pedro Acosta (Red Bull KTM Factory Racing) had a quiet and unassuming session with fourth, just ahead of Marc Marquez and Diggia. Quartararo booked his place in Q2 with P7, ahead of Alex Marquez, a late charge from Morbidelli and a salvaging effort from Bagnaia. MISSING THE CUT: Rins and Miller a tenth out Just missing the cut by 0.090s was Rins, with Miller likewise less than a tenth away from the top ten. Ogura is also in Q1 with P13 on Friday afternoon, ahead of Luca Marini (Honda HRC Castrol), Aldeguer and Toprak Razgatlioglu (Prima Pramac Yamaha MotoGP). Moreira and Bastianini, after their falls, also headline in what is set to be an action-packed Q1 on Saturday. Watch every session LIVE or OnDemand with MotoGP VideoPass, now 75% OFF!

signals.title: WorldSBK rookie Surra shines with a pair of Estoril podiums on Sunday: “I’m happy to keep improving and taking good results”
signals.summary: The #67 broke open the 2026 top rookie debate wide open as he leaves Estoril with a trio of bronze medals Rookie rider Alberto Surra (Motocorsa Racing) closed the MOTUL FIM Superbike World Championship with even more pace on Sunday. Not content with bagging his second podium of the season in the Tissot Estoril Round’s Race 1, the #67 sent the round out with a bang, taking two more rostrum results. Now with a tally of four, he sits tied with fellow WorldSBK rookie Miguel Oliveira (ROKiT BMW Motorrad WorldSBK Team) with four podiums apiece as they pack their bags for the season’s final round at the Circuito de Jerez - Angel Nieto, Andalucia. Surra hit the ground running on Saturday in the Tissot Superpole session and the opening Race 1 , and On Sunday he set off from third place in the Tissot Superpole Race. Miguel Oliveira (ROKiT BMW Motorrad WorldSBK Team) rode with a knife between his teeth at home into the opening corner, emerging in P3 behind Nicolo Bulega (Aruba.it Racing - Ducati) and Iker Lecuona (Aruba.it Racing - Ducati) while Surra fell as far as P5 behind an aggressive Jake Dixon (Honda HRC) on Turn 2. The #67 dispelled the factory Honda rider later that lap, but closing the one-second gap to the MotoGP-race-winning #88 would be a taller order for the young Italian. He settled into the race and by Lap 8, the margin was down to around six tenths. With a lap to go, it was just a tenth separating them, and when Oliveira made a mistake on the final lap, Surra found a way past on Turn 4 to cruise to his third rostrum result of the season. On his Superpole Race, Surra was pleased to have beaten out the #88, but was complimentary about his adversary. He said: “It’s been one of the best weekends of the season! I’m very happy; it was a very solid week for my team and me, and now we’ll go to Jerez. It’s a difficult circuit for my riding style, but I’m happy to keep improving and taking a good result for me and the team. Oliveira is a very fast rider, but I took P3 from him at Turn 4 in the Superpole Race. I’m really happy about that.” The Italian youngster can take a list of positives away from the weekend, including fighting with some of the paddock's biggest names The final race of the round saw Surra lock horns with a legend of the WorldSBK paddock: two-time WorldSBK Champion Alvaro Bautista (Barni Spark Racing Team). The #19 passed Surra for P3 on the opening lap, before the #67 took back his third-place grid start position on Lap 2 at Turn 6. Surra held the final podium spot until Lap 13, when he ran wide into the heavy-braking Turn 1, and the Spaniard sailed past him. Surra held the gap ahead of him to just three tenths by Lap 16, and a last lap fight for the podium looked to be in the cards, but an unfortunate crash from the #19 at Turn 1 on Lap 17 promoted the Italian up to P3, handing him his first-ever WorldSBK hat-trick On his final race of the round, and looking ahead to the season finale at Jerez, Surra said: “In Race 2 I had very good grip on the rear tyre, and I had the possibility to pass Alvaro, but then he crashed in Turn 1. I’m full of confidence for Jerez; it will be difficult, but I will fight for the best result for me and my team.” Tune in for the final races of Surra’s rookie campaign with action kicking off on Friday, October 16 th on the WorldSBK VideoPass! signals.title: Takahira Crowned First Japanese FIM Yamaha R3 BLU CRU World Cup Champion
signals.summary: Takahira’s comeback was completed as he claimed the title after a stunning season finale at Estoril Riichi Takahira made history at Circuito Estoril today, becoming the first Japanese rider to be crowned FIM Yamaha R3 BLU CRU World Cup Champion after a dramatic season finale. Just four points separated Takahira from title rival Xarly Mendez (Dominican Republic) heading into the finale. Saturday’s winner, Aymon Bocanegra (Brazil), also remained in contention if both leading riders failed to finish. Mendez had led the championship for much of the season before Takahira took the lead at the previous round in Cremona. After finishing sixth on Saturday, Mendez began the final race four points adrift of his rival. However, his title hopes ended three laps in when he crashed at Turn 7. He rejoined and completed the race, but finished outside the points. Takahira’s debut season began modestly at Balaton Park, where he recorded two seventh-place finishes. He soon reached the podium, finishing second in Round 2 at Aragón, before igniting his title challenge with a commanding double victory at Magny-Cours in Round 4. Another win at Cremona moved him into the championship lead ahead of the final round. Fourth place in Race 1 and seventh in Race 2 at Estoril were enough to secure the 2026 FIM Yamaha R3 BLU CRU World Cup title. Attention now turns to securing him a Yamaha-supported place in the 2027 FIM Sportbike World Championship. Despite the crash, Mendez retained second place in the championship, while Brazil’s Aymon Bocanegra moved into third overall after adding a third-place finish to Saturday’s victory. Chris Clark (USA) won the final race of the season, with Emanuele Pastore (Italy) finishing second. Riichi Takahira - 2026 FIM Yamaha R3 BLU CRU World Cup Champion said: “I am so happy to win the championship. The race was very crazy, so I tried my best to get the best result possible. It has been an incredible season. Thank you to all of my family and everyone who has supported me.”

signals.title: SUNDAY WARM UP: WorldSBK’s push to the finish in Estoril begins on Sunday with Lecuona leading Bulega and Baldassarri
signals.summary: The #7 started the final day on top in 2026’s final day in Portugal The MOTUL FIM Superbike World Championship shook down their machines ahead of the final day of racing at the Circuito Estoril, and Iker Lecuona (Aruba.it Racing - Ducati) found a strong feeling with his Ducati Panigale V4R machine right away. Teammate Nicolo Bulega (Aruba.it Racing - Ducati) finished in second, his best time just a hundredth behind the #7, while Lorenzo Baldassarri (Team GoEleven) took P3. Bulega will break yet another record this season if he can win one more WorldSBK race, as he tied Alvaro Bautista's (Barni Spark Racing Team) WorldSBK record of 27 wins in a single season with his Race 1 victory. Looking to beat his 2026 World Championship-winning teammate in Sunday’s races, Lecuona set a session-topping 1’34.973s, a sliver ahead of the #11 in P2 and his time of 1’34.983s. Four tenths behind the #11, Baldassarri is fixing for his first podium since Balaton Park, a result also scored in a Tissot Superpole Race. A podium would be just what the doctor ordered for the #34 as he looks to break into the top five, currently 21 points behind Sam Lowes (ELF Marc VDS Racing Team) in the Championship standings. Alberto Surra (Motocorsa Racing) sent himself up to the fight near the front once again to finish the Warm Up at in fourth place. While his session didn’t quite have the drama of another incredible save shown in FP3 , Yari Montella finished in an improved P5 compared to his Race 1 eighth-place result. Behind them, Alex Lowes (bimota by Kawasaki Racing Team) finished as the top non-Ducati, a mere three thousandths behind the #5. Axel Bassani (bimota by Kawasaki Racing Team) tailed his teammate on the timesheets from P7, 0.167s behind the Brit and 0.671s behind Lecuona at the front. Alvaro Bautista (Barni Spark Racing Team) crossed the line in P8, one position ahead of his Race 1 finish as the two-time World Champion Spaniard looks for a strong result to score himself a 2027 seat . Sam Lowes (ELF Marc VDS Racing Team) and Garrett Gerloff (Kawasaki WorldSBK Team) rounded off the top ten in that order, the transatlantic duo separated by just over a tenth. signals.title: RECORD BREAKER: Bulega takes historic 28th win of 2026 as Surra denies Oliveira dream home rostrum
signals.summary: Bulega took advantage of an error from Lecuona, who finished P2, while Surra claimed P3 after a last-lap battle with Oliveira Nicolo Bulega (Aruba.it Racing - Ducati) made more MOTUL FIM Superbike World Championship history with a 28 th win of the 2026 campaign. He won the Tissot Superpole Race at the Circuito Estoril ahead of teammate Iker Lecuona, while Alberto Surra (Motocorsa Racing) snatched third place from home hero Miguel Oliveira (ROKiT BMW Motorrad WorldSBK Team) on the final lap at the Tissot Estoril Round. Lecuona got a sensational start when the race got underway as he claimed the lead at Turn 1, while Yari Montella (Barni Spark Racing Team) made an aggressive move at the opening corner, making contact with Alex Lowes (bimota by Kawasaki Racing Team), with both dropping down the order, which allowed Oliveira to move into a provisional podium spot, slotting in behind polesitter Bulega. Montella was given a Long Lap Penalty for irresponsible riding. At the start of Lap 3, Lecuona had a huge moment under braking at Turn 1 and ran wide, allowing his teammate to take the lead and allowing Oliveira to challenge for P2; the #7 just held on. That gave Bulega breathing room at the head of the field as he claimed a record-breaking 28 th win of the season, beating the previous best set by Alvaro Bautista (Barni Spark Racing Team) in 2023 when he won 27 times. Lecuona claimed his 30 th WorldSBK podium, 28 of which have come this season. In the fight for third, it looked like Oliveira had the rostrum covered but Surra put on a late spurt to claim third after passing the BMW star at Turn 3 on Lap 10, with Oliveira unable to respond across the rest of the final lap. That gave Surra his third podium in the last four races. Bautista made quick progress in the early stages of the 10-lap race, launching up to the top five and remaining there for his first top five finish since the Balaton Park Superpole Race. Axel Bassani (bimota by Kawasaki Racing Team) was another who had a great start and he eventually finished the race in sixth place, keeping in touch with Bautista but unable to get close enough to pass. It means the second row for Race 2 will be Oliveira, Bautista and Bassani. Bulega was victorious after a mistake from Lecuona, while Oliveira was denied a dream home rostrum Xavi Vierge (Pata Maxus Yamaha) will line up from the third row for this afternoon’s Race 2 after claiming seventh ahead of Jake Dixon (Honda HRC), with the #96 losing one place compared to his starting position but securing an all-important top nine finish. Lorenzo Baldassarri (Team GoEleven) rounded out the top nine, with Sam Lowes (ELF Marc VDS Racing Team) missing out on a third-row start in Race 2 as he finished in P10. With both Alex Lowes and Montella dropping down the order, they both lose out on the Race 2 grid. The #22 will start from 10 th while Montella will line up from P11 in the final race of the weekend in Portugal. signals.title: MORE HISTORY MADE: Bulega beats long-standing Rea points record with Race 2 victory at Estoril
signals.summary: Bulega has now scored more points than anyone else in a single WorldSBK campaign after his Estoril treble Nicolo Bulega (Aruba.it Racing - Ducati) continues to make MOTUL FIM Superbike World Championship history with victory in Race 2 of the Tissot Estoril Round. The #11 beat teammate Iker Lecuona by just under five seconds for his latest win, while there was late podium drama at the Circuito Estoril. Alberto Surra (Motocorsa Racing) completed a hat-trick of P3 finishes in Portugal after a late crash for Alvaro Bautista (Barni Spark Racing Team). On the opening lap, Lecuona took the lead of the race, but Bulega made an aggressive move at Turn 6 on Lap 1 to reclaim the lead of the race before immediately starting to build a gap over his teammate. Although Lecuona initially stayed within half-a-second of his teammate, a 1’34.696s enabled ‘Bulegas’ to build a gap over his teammate in the first half of the race as he went on to secure a 29 th victory of the season, and it also means the 25 points he gained put his 2026 tally to 664 points – the highest tally in a single season, beating Jonathan Rea's 2019 tally of 663 with three races to go. He also has 33 podiums in 2026, with the all-time record for rostrums in a season standing at 34, set by Rea in 2019. Lecuona claimed his 31 st WorldSBK rostrum, with 25 of those being P2 finishes. In the fight for third, Bautista jumped up the order from fifth to run in third but an in-form Surra at Turn 6 on Lap 2, and their battle continued into Turn 1 on Lap 3; Surra retained the podium place. Bautista then had to resist Axel Bassani (bimota by Kawasaki Racing Team), which allowed Surra to build a gap over the chasing pack. However, once Bautista stabilised his pace, he started putting pressure on the #67 once again in the early stages, although the rookie was able to keep the two-time WorldSBK Champion at bay across the first half of the 21-lap race. By Lap 12, Bautista was all over the back of the rookie, and on Lap 13 the #19 was in P3 when Surra went wide at Turn 1. On the same lap, Surra answered back at Turn 6, but Bautista was able to respond immediately. However, a Lap 17 crash for Bautista at Turn 1 cost him a potential podium and promoted Surra back onto the rostrum. The two-time Champion was running in third but crashed out at Turn 1 Montella battled from 11 th on the grid to finish fourth, and, coupled with Sam Lowes (ELF Marc VDS Racing Team) finishing in 15 th he secured the 2026 Independent Riders’ title – the third year in a row a Barni Ducati rider has won it. With the #5 also outscoring his rivals for P3 in the standings, he has a 53-point advantage heading to Jerez in the battle for bronze. Bassani finished the race in fifth place after managing a gap to Lorenzo Baldassarri (Team GoEleven), with ‘Balda’ coming home in a relatively lonely sixth place. Garrett Gerloff (Kawasaki WorldSBK Team) finished in P7 as he fended off a hard-charging Miguel Oliveira (ROKiT BMW Motorrad WorldSBK Team). After starting from P4, the #88 was running as low as 14 th on the opening lap after he ran wide at Turn 6. From there, he fought his way through the field – passing Alex Lowes (bimota by Kawasaki Racing Team) and Gerloff in one move at Turn 1 on Lap 6 for P9, and attempting a similar move two laps later on Baldassarri and Xavi Vierge (Pata Maxus Yamaha), although he was only able to get ahead of ‘Balda’. On Lap 9, Oliveira ran wide at Turn 1 trying to pass his rivals and fell to 11 th , before eventually finishing in eighth. Vierge was classified in ninth with Jake Dixon (Honda HRC) rounding out the top ten. Estoril once again provided plenty of action as this year's visit concluded in style Tommy Bridewell (Superbike Advocates) finished in 11 th , half-a-second down on his fellow Brit in P10, while Remy Gardner (GYTR GRT Yamaha WorldSBK Team) finished in 12 th . The #87 had to fend off Somkiat Chantra (Honda HRC) on the final lap, with the Thai star just 0.033s behind the Australian rider at the end of the race. Stefano Manzi (GYTR GRT Yamaha WorldSBK Team) was 14 th with Sam Lowes picking up the final point with 15 th . Danilo Petrucci (ROKiT BMW Motorrad WorldSBK Team) finished in 16 th place, almost five seconds down on the #14 ahead. Mattia Rato (Motoxracing WorldSBK Team) and teammate Twan Smits were 17 th and 18 th respectively, as the last classified riders. Alex Lowes crashed out of the race on Lap 16 at Turn 4, while Loris Baz (MGM Optical Express Racing) crashed at Turn 3 a lap later. Andrea Locatelli (Pata Maxus Yamaha) also didn’t finish the race after bringing his bike into the pits with a technical issue. The top six from WorldSBK Race 2, full results here : Next up, Jerez! signals.title: Bulega on his latest accolades at Estoril: “It’s not that I don’t care about records… however, winning is more important”
signals.summary: The WorldSBK 2026 Riders’ Champion took another hat trick in Round 11, putting an exclamation point on his dominant campaign A MOTUL FIM Superbike World Championship trophy earned last round looks to have done little to dull Nicolo Bulega's (Aruba.it Racing - Ducati) insatiable appetite for silverware as he ran roughshod over the field at the Tissot Estoril Round. His teammate Iker Lecuona prevented ‘Bulegas’ from standing on the top step of the rostrum across all three of his home races at Cremona, but now with the title in hand and the pressure lifted from his shoulders, Bulega took the single-season race win record from his former teammate Alvaro Bautista (Barni Spark Racing Team). The #11 raised it to 29 wins with three races remaining at Jerez as he set the record for most hat tricks with 12 WorldSBK triples The #11 topped both Friday Free Practices and earned his 10 th pole position start with an emphatic circuit record-setting 1’33.884s to outpace his teammate in P2 by more than eight tenths. Saturday’s Race 1 was spic and span from the #11. He recovered the race lead with the event’s fastest lap time of 1’34.964 on Lap 3 after falling as far as third, behind Lecuona and Alex Lowes (bimota by Kawasaki Racing Team). He set fastest times through all sectors but the first, where he was less than a tenth off from the #7. The Italian continues to break records and is now the rider with the most points and wins in a single WorldSBK season In a blustery Sunday morning Tissot Superpole Race, the Italian saw his teammate once again enjoy a better jump off the line, leading by 0.113s after the opening lap. The Spaniard then narrowly extended his lead by a matter of thousandths over Lap 2, but after a big moment on the brakes into Turn 1 of Lap 3, Bulega again struck to take back the lead. A subsequent race lap record-setting 1’34.525s lap on Lap 4 carved out a margin of over 1.8 seconds on the #7, and while Lecuona would narrow that gap to cross the finish line just seven tenths behind the 2026 Champion, Bulega made it two for two at Estoril on Sunday morning. For the third and final time of the weekend, Lecuona again took the lead from the #11 on the run into the opening corner. Bulega got his revenge for later that lap at Turn 6, and left the rest of the pack in the dust from that point on. He opened Lap 2 with a two-tenth gap and took a tenth each lap over the next two laps to nurse a gap of nearly half a second by Lap 4. His margin stagnated at around a second and a half from Lap 9 to Lap 11, but he put the hammer down over the second half of the race to cross the line just shy of five seconds before his teammate. On his three-win weekend, Bulega said: “I’m really happy. An amazing Sunday and an amazing weekend overall, maybe even one of the best of the season because of how good my feeling with the bike was. My pace on Sunday in Race 2 was incredible, it was very, very fast. Iker was close to me at the beginning of the race, but then I continued to push and my pace over the second half of the race was a bit better. I managed the tyre a bit better, so I’m really happy about my performance and what my team was able to do because they improved the bike a lot.” Having locked down all three titles in 2026, Bulega continues to swing for the fences in 2026 as he hunts down what few records he hasn’t stamped his, and his manufacturers’ name atop already. His Race 1 win saw him land his 47 th career win in the class, the 480 th for Ducati. With P1 in Race 2, he closed to within one rostrum result of tying Jonathan Rea's record-holding 34-podium 2019 season; yet the Ulsterman did see his name replaced atop another record tally on Sunday afternoon, as with the 25 points from P1, Bulega passed Rea’s record 663-point 2019 season. The Italian currently holds 664 after Estoril with three races still left to ride. While he typically downplays the significance of these accolades to the media, Bulega got candid on Sunday afternoon; he said: “It’s fantastic, it’s not that I don’t care about records; I do care. It makes me really proud to achieve records and see my name on top of these lists; at the end of the day however, to me winning races is more important. I’m already thinking about Jerez and if I can raise the records even higher.“ Tune in for 2026’s final round at Jerez on October 16th with the WorldSBK VideoPass! Now just €9.99!

signals.title: Alcoba wins red-flagged WorldSSP Race 2 at Estoril in tricky conditions, foiling Farioli and ZXMOTO’s Debise
signals.summary: The fight for third in the Championship standings is heating up with three riders within five points as Oncu overtakes Masia With a new FIM Supersport World Champion crowned in Race 1, the class attacked their red-flagged final race at the Circuito Estoril. Rain began to fall on track in the opening laps on Sunday afternoon, and after the red flags waved for track conditions after a crash, Jeremy Alcoba (Kawasaki WorldSSP Team) crossed the line first in the restarted six-lap race, bagging his third win in four races. Filippo Farioli (VFT Racing Yamaha) took P2 at the final race of the Tissot Estoril Round for his second podium in the last five races, ahead of Valentin Debise (EASTROC ZXMOTO Factory Evan Bros Racing), who took a composed bronze medal to clinch second place in the Riders’ Championship. Roberto Garcia (GMT94 Yamaha) shot off from pole to take the holeshot, tailed by Debise, Farioli and Tom Booth-Amos (PTR Triumph Factory Racing). Garcia led the race as rain began to fall, until Can Oncu (Pata Yamaha Ten Kate Racing) clipped the Spaniard’s leg on the run into Turn 1 of Lap 6, sending the #37 wide and later to the medical centre, where he was ruled unfit with a contusion and sprain to his right knee. Moments later, on the same lap, Booth-Amos slipped past the Turk but lost the front and crashed out of the lead in the increasingly wet conditions. With 10 laps remaining, the sun began to reappear as Farioli led the race ahead of Lucas Mahias (GMT94 Yamaha) and Oncu. The next lap, however, brought red flags for track conditions after Bahattin Sofuoglu (QJMOTOR Factory Racing) crashed out at Turn 3, sending dirt, dust, and fluids from the bike onto the tarmac. Oncu took zero prisoners on Sunday, cutting inside for the holeshot from quite a distance behind Farioli and Mahias. The #94 saw his time fighting at the front come to an end, however, as he ran wide at Turn 4 and Alcoba seized the opportunity as he took P1 from Farioli on the run into Turn 1 with three laps to go. Farioli hung in within half a second of the Spaniard, but the shortened race distance didn’t leave the Italian much time to take his revenge. Alcoba ran away with Race 2 to land his third win in four races. While Farioli couldn’t quite strike back in Race 2 for his first win in the class, he has been a revelation in the late rounds of his sophomore 2026 season and P2 spells his best result in the class so far. Debise set off from P6 after the restart and came out the victor in a no-holds-barred battle with Oncu for a ninth podium this season. Despite aggressive attack after attack into Turn 1, the Turkish rider finished off the podium in P4. He has an important final round to come at Jerez, as Alcoba and Jaume Masia (Orelac Racing VerdNatura) now sit just five points behind the #61 for third in the Riders’ Championship. Like Oncu, Mahias ran up near the front for most of the race, but the Frenchman dropped to P5 for the second time in the round. German rider Philipp Oettl (Feel Racing WorldSSP Team) took P6 for his best result of the past three rounds, just a tenth ahead of Matteo Ferrari (WRP Racing). The Italian’s P7 helped right the ship after a costly Race 1 DNF saw him fall behind Oettl in the Riders’ Championship standings, now in ninth place. Dominique Aegerter (Kawasaki WorldSSP Team) finished P8 on Sunday after a P14 start following the red flag. He can be happy with his performance at Estoril; while he took a P24 finish in Race 1, he was riding in the top ten in the opening race as well. Ever-consistent Mattia Casadei (D34G WorldSSP Racing Team) finished in his same grid start position after the restart in P9, tying his third-best result so far in 2026. Closing out the top ten, Spanish rider Borja Jimenez (WRP Racing) took his best result of his rookie WorldSSP season in P10. The rider from Murcia has enjoyed his time at Estoril, scoring points in both races for the first time in his WorldSSP career. Sporadic rain, fierce fights and an epic scrap were the order of the WorldSSP day at Estoril Eight riders ended Sunday early in the tricky conditions: Aldi Mahendra (AS BLU CRU Racing Team), Jaume Masia (Orelac Racing VerdNatura), Eric Fernandez (Cerba Yamaha Racing Team), Tom Booth-Amos, Bahattin Sofuoglu, all crashed out, as well as Albert Arenas (AS BLU CRU Racing Team), who saw his race end before the red flag with a tech issue at Turn 1. All riders were ruled fit apart from Masia after his crash with Fernandez, the #5 was diagnosed with a fracture of the second metatarsal on his left foot. Oliver Konig (Compos Racing Team) and Roberto Garcia (GMT94 Yamaha) also retired from the race. Top six from WorldSSP Race 2: Full results here! signals.title: Victory preserves Bocanegra’s title dreams in the penultimate race of the 2026 FIM Yamaha R3 BLU CRU World Cup.
signals.summary: The Brazilian still has a chance at the 11th hour with the World Cup on the line An important victory for Aymon Bocanegra in the first race of the weekend keeps the Brazilian rider’s dreams a possibility, as he crossed the line by just five-tenths of a second ahead of fellow countryman Mario Salles to take a crucial 25 points, leaving himself trailing Japan’s Riichi Takahira by 23 points heading into the final race of the year. Takahira, who qualified in eighth position, battled within the top 6 for the majority of the ten-lap race, and ultimately took the chequered flag in fourth place, which was enough to extend his title lead over rival Xarly Mendez to four points. Mendez made a strong start from pole position; however, despite leading five of the ten laps, the rider from the Dominican Republic lost on the final lap, eventually dropping to sixth. Italy’s Emanuele Pastore added to his 2026 podium tally with an impressive third-place finish, while Angelo Mottola rounded out the top five in the penultimate race of the year. It’s all to play for tomorrow, as the top three riders in the category are separated by just 23 points heading into what promises to be a thrilling battle for the very last race of the 2026 FIM Yamaha R3 BLU CRU World Cup. The final race of the year will get underway at 13:00 (Local Time UTC +1) and can be watched live on the Yamaha Racing YouTube channel here . On his win, Bocanegra said: “I’m super happy right now because I’m fighting to win the World Cup and now I’ve won this race, so tomorrow we see if we can win the championship.”

signals.title: “This title was super special… I want to enjoy this moment” – Arenas reflects on his 2026 WorldSSP Champion campaign
signals.summary: The #75 etched his name into the history books again as he hoists a second World Champion trophy after his 2020 Moto3 title Albert Arenas (AS BLU CRU Racing Team) is the FIM Supersport World Champion in his rookie campaign. The #75 secured the title in Race 1 at the Circuito Estoril with a rare finish off the podium, coming home in fourth place after a fierce fight at the front of the field. With title rival Valentin Debise (EASTROC ZXMOTO Evan Bros Factory) finishing sixth from 17 th on the grid, it was enough to wrap up the Championship with a round to spare. Arenas moved into the WorldSSP paddock this season with the AS BLU CRU Racing Team, with Andrea Quadranti’s team switching from MV Agusta machinery to Yamaha with Arenas and Aldi Mahendra. It was a switch that immediately paid off, with Arenas winning in Race 2 at Phillip Island in his debut weekend. From there, he claimed victories in Race 2 at Balaton Park and Race 2 at Misano, but it was his podium consistency that helped him to the title: 16 podiums from 21 races meant he held a significant advantage over Debise, despite the Frenchman winning twice as many races. Winning a world title isn't new for Arenas - but he reflected on what the second one meant to him after clinching the WorldSSP crown Arenas knew a podium finish would give him the title in Race 1 at Estoril regardless of Debise’s results and, despite starting from the third row, was immediately in podium contention – and fighting for victory too. On the last lap, he was getting involved in the fight for P1 with Tom Booth-Amos (PTR Triumph Factory Racing) and his teammate, Oli Bayliss, perhaps taking more risks than needed. Eventually, he lost out to Jeremy Alcoba (Kawasaki WorldSSP Team), finishing fourth, but securing the title despite Debise’s comeback. Discussing his title win, which is his second World Championship after Moto3 in 2020, Arenas said: “It feels so, so good, so special to give this title to my team, especially after they did such an incredible job all season. It’s amazing how much hard work they and Yamaha put in. It’s been super special to start from Race 1, getting the win then being able to be so consistent; I’m super, super happy about the achievement. It was a nice, nice Championship. I wanted to win this race, but there were two Triumph rocket ships. I gave it my 100% and it was a nice fight with contact. It was a bit of a hectic race, but happy to finish it and claim the title. The first title was incredible, and a childhood dream came true. This title was super special because I’m now much more conscious about what it means. It’s been building over the last year, working for it, and slowly starting to believe in it. It tastes really well. I want to enjoy this moment, but of course, I want to repeat it.” The Road Racing Sporting Manager at Yamaha Motor Europe reacts to Arenas' and the team's fantastic season It was a day of celebrations for Yamaha. Arenas’ result secured the Riders’ Championship for the second season in a row, while the Japanese brand also secured the Manufacturers’ Championship for the 12 th time. And, to cap off a memorable day, the AS BLU CRU Racing Team secured the Teams’ Championship after a long journey for Quadranti and his squad. Reflecting on Yamaha’s 2026 success, Nicolo Canepa, Road Racing Sporting Manager at Yamaha Motor Europe, said: “We’re super happy, I want to congratulate the team because they did a really fantastic job. They are new to Yamaha, so we started together at the beginning of the season and it wasn’t easy. Everything was last minute, but I’m truly amazed by the job they did during the whole season. We knew that Albert was our main rider to fight for the title and he really met that expectation. AS BLU CRU Racing Team Manager, Andrea Quadranti, reflects on his first ever world title in 11 years in the paddock An emotional Quadranti, Team Manager at AS BLU CRU Racing Team, added: “I have to say it’s kind of a strange feeling. When you win a race, the feeling is different. It’s like an explosion of adrenaline and satisfaction. In this case, maybe because we didn’t end up on the podium, I have this mixed feeling. It’s something that should make you happy because it’s much bigger than one win, which is something that happened somewhere else. It’s my first time as a World Champion. Maybe tomorrow, I’ll realise and appreciate it more. I chose Albert because I was convinced that he could do well, even though there were many tracks he didn’t know. This season was great. His way to stay focused on races throughout the Championship, without making mistakes, so we knew it could be an amazing season. The biggest part is Albert keeping cool when riding. If he sees he can’t win, he takes what he can out of it. Being consistent in this Championship is very important. I’m happy about the Teams’ Championship as well. It praises the hard work my team has done for many years.” Tune in for the final WorldSSP race at Estoril this season with Race 2 kicking off on Sunday at 14:00 (Local Time UTC +1)! signals.title: ROOKIE CHAMP: Arenas secures 2026 World Supersport crown after stellar campaign
signals.summary: The #75 has crowned himself 2026 WorldSSP Champion, the second-ever Spanish winner in the category. Albert Arenas (AS BLU CRU Racing Team) has closed out the 2026 FIM Supersport World Championship battle early after taking a P4 finish at the Circuito Estoril. The WorldSSP rookie’s breakout campaign bulldozed the competition as his podium consistency etched his name ever-present on the rostrum. His triumph this season was earned after fighting tooth and nail each round with a host of talented riders; going head-to-head with a record-setting nine different race winners. While runaway pace from rivals like Valentin Debise (EASTROC ZXMOTO Factory Evan Bros Racing) led him to more race wins this season than the #75, Arenas’s composure in the heat of battle saw him lock down podiums more consistently this season than any other rider. 16 podiums out of 21 races, including 11 P2s, with only three wins, proved too tall a challenge for his rivals to overcome as even when he was beaten for pace, he prevented strong swings in points. The #75 has been consistent throughout the year as he claimed his WorldSSP title Jaume Masia (Orelac Racing VerdNatura) came out of the gate firing on all cylinders over the first three rounds; while Arenas managed a win and three podiums over the first three rounds, he lurked behind his countryman in P2. The #75 picked his moment well at Balaton Park, seizing the title lead with a Race 1 P2 when Masia crashed out from the contest. Once he got his hands on P1, he sunk his teeth into the 2026 calendar. After a Race 1 bronze medal and a controversial Race 2 crash after contact with the #5 at Most, Arenas set off on a six-race streak placing at least P2, including a Race 2 win at Misano. That streak proved the difference, as while his rivals each had moments of brilliance, none could consistently emerge near the front race in, race out as Arenas. The emphatic nature of his trophy-lifting campaign makes it easy to forget that back in February, Arenas was riding in his maiden WorldSSP races as a rookie in the paddock . He was one of the most highly-anticipated rookies to have joined the paddock in recent memory; yet 2020 Moto3 World Championship or not, questions swirled pertaining to how he would acclimate to the paddock with such a weather-abridged preseason of testing. He would prove a fast learner however, and joins: Dominique Aegerter (Kawasaki WorldSSP Team), Andrea Locatelli (Pata Maxus Yamaha), Sandro Cortese, and Cal Crutchlow among the riders to have achieved a Supersport World Championship in their first full season. Reflecting on his 2026 success, Arenas said: “It feels so, so good, so special to give this title to my team, especially after they did such an incredible job all season. It’s amazing how much hard work they and Yamaha put in. I’m super, super happy about the achievement.” Arenas has been crowned in 2026, but there’s still more to come in 2026! signals.title: LAP RECORD SMASHED: Bulega breaks into the 1’33s bracket as he beats Lecuona to Estoril pole
signals.summary: The 2026 Champion set a 1’33.884s as he claimed his and Ducati’s first pole position at the Portuguese venue Nicolo Bulega (Aruba.it Racing - Ducati) claimed his first pole position at the Circuito Estoril in the MOTUL FIM Superbike World Championship ahead of teammate Iker Lecuona, while Alex Lowes (bimota by Kawasaki Racing Team) prevented an all-Ducati front row by putting his Bimota machine in third. Home hero Miguel Oliveira (ROKiT BMW Motorrad WorldSBK Team) goes from fifth at the Tissot Estoril Round after a record-breaking Tissot Superpole session. Oliveira laid down a gauntlet on his first run with a 1’34.651s, although Alberto Surra (Motocorsa Racing) did beat that on his first flying lap with a 1’34.511s as he moved into provisional pole. However, both times were immediately bettered by four tenths as Bulega set a new pole lap record with a 1’34.105s for P1. Lecuona was also able to get himself into the first row, provisionally demoting Oliveira onto the second row. As the second run got underway, Bulega was able to extend his advantage at the head of the field by going two tenths quicker to set a barely believable 1’33.884s to make it 10 poles from 11 this season, and claiming Ducati’s first pole at Estoril. Lecuona found time on his second run to set a 1’34.041s, under the previous lap record, to move into second. Alex Lowes had provisionally gone into second before Lecuona demoted him, but he was able to secure a front row start with third. Surra was unable to improve his time on his second run and he fell to fourth, narrowly missing out on a third front row start of the season. Oliveira will start from fifth place as he searches for more home rostrums after his three P3s at Portimao earlier in the season. Yari Montella (Barni Spark Racing Team) was unable to set a time in his second stint with the #5 after missing out on crossing the line before the chequered flag fell, but Montella will start from sixth; he set a 1’34.747s for a second row start. Discover how pole was decided at the Circuito Estoril! Jake Dixon (Honda HRC) followed Lecuona around as he set his best lap time, posting a 1’34.788s to secure his best Superpole result of this season as he’ll lead away the third row. Axel Bassani (bimota by Kawasaki Racing Team) will join the #96 in the top nine as he set a 1’34.839s, just half-a-tenth away from Dixon. Lorenzo Baldassarri (Team GoEleven) will go from ninth with Sam Lowes (ELF Marc VDS Racing Team) rounding out the top ten. signals.title: “I’m staying focused for my best results race by race” Surra strikes again at Estoril for first long race rostrum
signals.summary: The #67 is coming into his own in the late stages of his first-ever WorldSBK season Italian rookie Alberto Surra (Motocorsa Racing) is pushing full throttle to the end of his debut 2026 MOTUL FIM Superbike World Championship campaign. Round 10 at Cremona brought his maiden rostrum result in dramatic fashion at home , and the Tissot Estoril Round looks to be the next rung on the ascendant rookie’s ladder, as he took his first podium in a long race at the Circuito Estoril. Surra narrowly missed a spot in the front row after Alex Lowes (Bimota by Kawasaki Racing Team) set a time just eight hundredths faster than the Italian’s Tissot Superpole session time. Starting from P4 in the afternoon’s Race 1, he made hay early and passed the British Bimota rider on Lap 2 to take third place. He kept it clean from there, growing his one-second gap ahead of Miguel Oliveira (ROKiT BMW Motorrad WorldSBK Team) on Lap 4 to just shy of two seconds by Lap 12. A sign of further growth for the rookie was his race management: while he saw his pace decline sharply over the closing laps, particularly in long races, he went on to hold off the Portuguese MotoGP race winner in his home round and finish 1.8 seconds ahead of the #88. On his Race 1 podium, Surra said: “I’m really happy with my first podium in a long race. It’s even more emotional; it’s fantastic. I want to thank my team, they’re my second family. I have a great relationship with them. In this moment, I’ve been in a good mentality. Before Cremona, we improved the setup and something on the electronics. Now I have good feedback on the bike, and, step by step, I think another podium is possible. I don’t know if it will be at Estoril, but I know it’s possible.” The Italian rookie is not sure when, but he's confident he and his Motocorsa squad can find a spot on the podium again in 2026 With his sophomore seat already secured for 2027 , and all of the 2026 season’s titles already decided, Surra has a rare opportunity to ride free of pressure and attack the top positions over the final five races of the season. He feels the podium is well within his grasp and has proven it over the last two rounds, despite the best efforts of powerhouse riders Yari Montella (Barni Spark Racing Team) and Sam Lowes (ELF Marc VDS Racing Team). Keeping his feet on the ground, however, the young Italian was quick to keep expectations realistic as he doesn’t feel he has the pace to fight for the win against Nicolo Bulega (Aruba.it Racing - Ducati) and his teammate Iker Lecuona just yet. On his expectations for the rest of this season, and whether he feels a maiden win is in the cards in 2026, Surra said: “I don’t think a win is possible yet, but it’s still the dream, but I’m staying focused for my best results race by race. Nicolo and Iker still have a really good package, and they are really fast riders. I’m a rookie, so I want to keep going step by step.” Tune in Live and OnDemand to catch the impressive rookie’s final five races, and he will return on Sunday at Estoril in the Tissot Superpole Race, kicking off at 11:10 (Local Time UTC +1).
